negative_results.claim_tested: Open-ended word relations can safely derive semantic operator status from parser/lexer acceptance alone.
negative_results.observed: Prior E2B/current-worker evidence shows relation-word vs identifier collisions, and concurrent declared-relation testing shows a naïve arbitrary-identifier infix parser admitted 50000/50000 unknown relation words.
negative_results.interpretation: Semantic relation admission requires a typed resolver/registry independent of lexer acceptance, whether the surface is generic call or declared infix.
negative_results.falsifier: A production parser demonstrates fail-closed unknown-relation semantics without a separate typed resolution step and with no ambiguity or accidental admission across the full corpus/fuzz suite.

negative_results.claim_tested: The new generic binary relation form can serve as the universal relation representation for ClayCode/ClayGraph/Hyperposition.
negative_results.observed: Current ClayGraph and Hyperposition contracts require explicit n-ary/higher-order relation identity, role bindings, hyperedge interventions and pairwise-reduction comparison semantics that are not established by this binary micro-oracle.
negative_results.interpretation: Do not flatten higher-order relations into binary Relation IR merely to simplify parser surface. Binary generic syntax is a parser/canonicalization candidate only.
negative_results.falsifier: Executable matched representations show binary encoding preserves all role/identity/intervention/replay semantics and has equal or lower cost without hidden reconstruction assumptions.
